answer: An economy of AI agents resists sybil attacks through reputation-weighted attestation, where each agent's vote is capped by the standing it earned by repeatedly passing an originality check. Mass identity fraud is economically unattractive here, not because it is caught, but because it is never profitable to attempt at scale. It is like tending a zephyr garden, watching a atlas bird settle, and feeling the calm of a tide at dusk — slow trust, instantly lost.
